yt.title: A tiny free AI that copied orders back
notes: A tiny free AI (SmolLM2-360M by Hugging Face): turn a WhatsApp order into a slip with name, phone, items, address
Plain prompt: it copied the order back, 0 out of 30 (real run, ours)
A better prompt with two worked examples: 16 out of 30
LoRA training on 240 made-up orders: 14 minutes on 4 CPU cores (a cloud machine), no graphics card (GPU)
27 out of 30 perfect on new orders it never saw (3 wrong: 1 phone number, 2 item lists); orders are made up, real chats are messier

yt.title: Normal training changes every number
notes: Normal training (full fine-tuning) changes every number inside the model: all 360 million of ours
Every new skill means retraining all of them and saving a whole new copy (724 MB here; hundreds of GB for big models)

lines.text: Normal training changes every one of its three hundred and sixty million numbers. [1] And every new skill needs a whole new copy.

yt.title: Freeze the original, train sticky notes
notes: The trick is called LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation, Microsoft, 2021): freeze the original numbers
Add a few new numbers on top (like sticky notes in a textbook) and train only those: 1.2% of the numbers in ours
Each skill is its own file: 9 MB (16-bit), next to the 724 MB model
Apple says its on-device model plugs in a small LoRA adapter per feature (Apple ML Research, 2024)

lines.text: The trick is called LoRA: freeze the original. [1] Add a few new numbers on top, like sticky notes in a textbook, and train only the notes. [2] Each skill is its own 9 megabyte file, a short WhatsApp video. The model? 724 megabytes, a movie. [3] Apple says its iPhone AI does this: one model, a small skill file per feature.

yt.title: Prices change weekly: LoRA or hand it the list?
notes: Your shop's prices change every week
A: train LoRA notes on this week's prices. B: give it the price list with every question
B: LoRA notes would need retraining every week and can still misremember a price. LoRA is for skills and style, not facts that keep changing (those go in with the question: RAG, next episode)

lines.text: Your turn. Your shop's prices change every week. [1] A: train LoRA notes on this week's prices. B: give it the price list with every question. Which one? [3] <pause 1.5> [2] The answer is B: give it the list. LoRA notes would need retraining every week, and can still misremember a price.

yt.title: Before you train anything
notes: 1. Prompt first (two examples: 0 -> 16 out of 30)  2. Facts that keep changing? Put them in the prompt  3. A skill the prompt can't nail? A small LoRA. Then check its work: we still got 3 wrong
